tts: I had a bad experience the other day. I was having lunch with a friend in a café when a man came over and asked for directions to the station.
He put a map down on the table and my friend showed him where to go. I noticed that the man wasn’t listening carefully to my friend. He was looking nervously at the table.
So, anyway, a few minutes later I wanted to make a phone call, but I couldn’t find my phone.
You’re joking! Don’t tell me — the phone was on the table and the man lifted the map and took it.

How does the listener react?

acts.title: From: Dana. Subject: you will not believe this
text: Guess what — I finally went to see my brother in Astana last weekend, and it was a complete nightmare from beginning to end.

The train was supposed to leave at seven. While we were waiting on platform four, they announced a delay of forty minutes. Then an hour. Then they cancelled it. There was no other train until the morning, so about two hundred of us were standing in one queue trying to change our tickets at the same time.

I got a bus in the end. I was sleeping when we stopped somewhere at three in the morning, and I woke up because a complete stranger was sitting on my luggage. He was very apologetic. There was nowhere else to sit.
Anyway, I arrived at nine, eleven hours late, and my brother had already left for work. I sat on his step for two hours and I was not in a good mood.
The strange part: it was the best weekend I have had this year. We laughed about the journey the whole time.
How was your week? Write back soon.

items.q: What time was the train supposed to leave?
What happened to the train in the end?
Why was there a queue?

o: a stranger sitting on her luggage

items.q: How late did she arrive?
What does she say about the weekend overall?

it was the worst this year

sub.en: These are the parts of the email. Put them in the order Dana used.

items.a: Open with Dear and the name
Say the big news in one line
Move to the end with Anyway
Ask about them and sign off

write.q: Write an informal email about a journey or a day when everything went wrong: 8–10 lines. Follow the model’s six parts, and use at least four of its phrases: Dear… / Guess what / While I was… / In the end / Anyway / Write back soon.
write.model: Dear Marat, Guess what — I finally tried to get to the airport by bus and it was a disaster. While I was standing at the stop, the app changed the arrival time four times. In the end I took a taxi, and the driver was learning the route from a map on his knee. We were going the wrong way for twenty minutes before I noticed. Anyway, I got there forty minutes before the gate closed and I have never run so fast in my life. The strange part is that I would do it again. How was your week? Write back soon. Aigul

speak.q: Tell your story out loud in five sentences: open it, set the scene with “While I was …-ing”, give two events, finish with “In the end…”. Then react to this: “They cancelled my flight and there was nothing until Tuesday.”
speak.model: You’ll never believe what happened. While I was waiting at the bus stop, the app changed the time four times. In the end I took a taxi and the driver got lost. Anyway, I arrived forty minutes before the gate closed. — That’s awful! What a nightmare. Poor you.
